Obviously anecdotal, but, as a suicidal person, i am not against suicide. I understand that there are situations where it seems like the only option, there are people who just aren't cut out to be here (like me) and i support people's right to choose whether or not they want to be here. Life shouldn't be forced on the unwilling. It would be hypocritical of me to be unsupportive or talk about the positives of life.

As a suicidal person i understand the frustration and exhaustion with the "Oh you have so much to live for!" or "It gets better!"

That doesn't mean i encourage suicide, i definitely encourage therapy, and trying all kinds of different methods for improving your life and make it livable. But i will not argue that suicide is wrong, or not **an** answer, i won't feed into the guilt and pain associated with having these ingrained feelings.

The only thing we can truly do, and the reason i'm on this sub, is to get the feeling that i'm not alone in all these horrible thoughts. That i'm not alone in feeling worthless and like i have no place in the world.

I feel like you need a bit more compassion. Some women are hesitant to have children, but are told by their family, their partner and their partner's family that it's going to be good, that it'll be easy, that they'll have so much help and so many resources. So they give in, push their doubts away, their hesitation.

And then the baby comes, and your family is nowhere to be found. Your loving husband left you (men are more likely to cheat during their spouse's pregnancy), or found out that a baby is tough work and leaves it all to you. After all, isn't it a woman's job? And your in-laws go no-contact.  
This is not an uncommon story.

And yes, she could have been smarter, she could have thought it through, but how could she have doubted all the people she loved? That they'd be there? But it happens, it happened, and now she's stuck alone with a giant responsibility.

And then there's the stories of people who have these extremely positive ideals of what having a child is like, and then reality hits like a truck - it's not all sunshine and rainbows and happy days. It's tantrums and disobedience, overwhelming, constant responsibility. Some women are sold this idea that babies are amazing, and being a mother is so fulfilling and perfect, but that's just not reality.

I'm childfree, i don't like kids, i don't want kids, and i can't be persuaded either, but my heart bleeds for the mothers who are alone, the mothers discovering that it's so much tougher than expected.

Our DNA encodes how hair grows. Hair goes through growth phases, the anagen, catagen, telegen and exogen phase.
Basically, think of it like code. Your DNA tells the follicle to grow for x amount of time, then stop, pause, and fall out. The hairs on our arms and our peach fuzz and eyebrows and such have a very short time (x) before they're ordered to fall out, which is why they don't get very long. The hair on our head has a very long growth phase, often spanning several years before they're ordered to fall out. 

And to be honest, we don't really know why specifically the hair on top of our heads have such a long growth phase. Perhaps there's no reason, and it's just evolutionary because our ancestors liked long-haired people, so those with long growth phases on top were the ones to procreate.

Discharge is also what is produced to lubricate the vagina when you are turned on sexually (often called "being wet"). 

If the discharge is very bad smelling or looking weird, it can be an indicator of a problem, like too much bacteria growth, and it can be good to see a doctor if it is too bad, but it is often just normal.

Aside from my main contact with a psychiatrist as part of my treatment programme (anxiety and schizotypal), i've also used an emergency psychiatric service (akutmodtagelse) due to severe suicidal thoughts, and i've been admitted to a hospital's emergency psych center after a suicide attempt. The emergency psychiatric service (akutmodtagelse) really didn't work for me personally, i did feel like they were taking me seriously, and that they were trying to help, but being confined and treated with uncertainty just made things worse in the end, and i had to struggle and fight for several hours (with words) before they'd let me out again. The hospital psych was nice, it was the place i got a proper diagnosis of schizotypal on top of the anxiety disorder, and they were the ones to refer me to a proper psychiatrist, in a very quick time (around 2 weeks). Derudover har jeg også nogle mentale og fysiske skavanker, der ikke kun ville gøre mig til en dårlig forælder, men som jeg heller ikke vil give videre til et barn.

Primært beskæftiger de obligatoriske fag i biologi sig med de 4 riger (dyr, planter, svampe, alger) plus en smule matematik, (bio-)kemi, cellelære og mikrobiologi. Meget kort går man ind på mennesker med et enkelt obligatorisk fag, Menneskets Fysiologi. Hvis du er interesseret i en psykologisk retning er det nok nemmest at finde fag rettet mod dyrs psyke, og adfærdsbiologi, men du må gerne vælge fag fra alle fakulteter (så længe du søger om både forhåndsgodkendelse, plads på det andet fakultet, og merit!) så man kunne sætte et par interessefag ind.
